claims.text: Aging the solution-treated Nb–Ti–Al–Zr refractory HEA at approximately 600°C for 2–4 hours will produce coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates.
The L12 precipitates will form a uniform dispersion within the alloy matrix.
The nanoscale L12 precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion by Orowan bowing.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
The aged alloy will have approximately 20–30% higher yield strength at about 1000 K than the as-solutionized alloy.
The proposed high-temperature benefit is expected under both quasi-static and dynamic loading.
The aging treatment will preserve room-temperature ductility.
The aging treatment will maintain room-temperature strength and other mechanical properties at levels similar to the as-solutionized baseline.
The aging treatment and resulting precipitation will not significantly affect alloy density, so the alloy will remain low-density.
Systematic optimization of aging temperature and time can control precipitate coarsening.
Departures from the specified aging window or alloy composition may cause inadequate precipitation control or adverse mechanical behavior.
The long-term stability of the precipitates under cyclic high-temperature loading is uncertain.
